steps.what: Provide dermatologic consultation after reviewing clinical records and assessing the colleague's clinical question

tasks.design: The dermatologist reviews the clinical record system {OTHER} and relevant guidance in {DOCS}, then discusses the colleague's question. Record access supports specialist judgement without substituting a generated answer for the consultation.
tasks.previous_blocker: The question may depend on incomplete history and examination context.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing clinical records and guidance support specialist review.
tasks.still_hard: Interpret uncertain findings and communicate appropriately qualified advice.
tasks.human_edge: Understand the clinical question and judge what evidence is missing.
tasks.altitude: Own the quality of specialist consultation.

evidence.claim: Specialist dermatologic consultation retains its clinical review and discussion time in this design.

assumptions: The task boundary is clinical consultation rather than a separate documentation workload.
The clinical record system {OTHER} remains unchanged and no new data extraction or diagnostic tool is proposed.
Existing record access and documents suffice, with no additional automation upkeep.
unknowns: Consultation format and available clinical evidence
research_questions: Is there a distinct recurring information-assembly workload outside the consultation itself?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net 0. Clinical interpretation and colleague discussion remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Instruct interns and residents through case discussion, observation and clinical practice feedback

tasks.design: The dermatologist teaches from actual cases and approved material in {DOCS}. Case discussion, observation and corrective feedback retain their time rather than being replaced by generated teaching text.
tasks.previous_blocker: Clinical learning depends on the trainee's reasoning and observed practice.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing case materials support direct teaching.
tasks.still_hard: Recognize mistaken reasoning and adapt supervision.
tasks.human_edge: Connect clinical observation with tailored feedback.
tasks.altitude: Own trainee development and clinical understanding.

reach.task: Teach recognition of dermatological referral needs

evidence.claim: Clinical instruction and feedback retain full human time in this design.

assumptions: No high-volume slide-writing or examination-marking workload is invented inside clinical instruction.
Existing teaching documents suffice; no new system maintenance is introduced.
research_questions: Which preparation activities are repetitive and distinct from required clinical teaching?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net 0. Teaching, observation and feedback remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Conduct clinical or basic dermatology research

steps.what: Define clinical or basic research questions, methods and appropriate study arrangements
Conduct research observations and analyze findings within the defined study approach

tasks.design: Keep study design, observations and scientific interpretation with the dermatologist and existing research team. {DOCS} and {SPREADSHEET} support the study; the broad task statement establishes no repeated extraction or calculation package to automate.
tasks.previous_blocker: Research methods and data depend on the scientific question.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing research tools support a defined study.
tasks.still_hard: Design valid methods and interpret uncertain findings.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish useful evidence from methodological artifacts.
tasks.altitude: Own the validity and relevance of dermatology research.

evidence.claim: Clinical and basic research retain their time unless a specific repeatable subtask and data contract are established.

assumptions: This baseline covers focal dermatologist research effort; other researchers' existing work is not converted into dermatologist savings.
No new study approvals or data-use authority are created by this design.
Existing research tools remain and no new automation upkeep is introduced.
unknowns: Study type and repeated computational workload
research_questions: Which observed research calculations or extraction steps recur under the same validated protocol?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net 0. Study design, observations and interpretation retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Evaluate patients using clinical records, examination and discussion to determine cosmetic procedure eligibility

tasks.design: The dermatologist evaluates history in the clinical record system {OTHER}, examines the patient and discusses goals and alternatives. Guidance in {DOCS} supports the assessment without generating an eligibility flag or promising a particular outcome.
tasks.previous_blocker: Suitability depends on clinical findings, risks and individual expectations.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing records and guidance support a complete assessment.
tasks.still_hard: Weigh risks, realistic benefit and patient expectations.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize when an intervention is unsuitable and explain why.
tasks.altitude: Own individualized suitability decisions and clear communication.

reach.task: Clarify patient concerns before specialist assessment

evidence.claim: Cosmetic-procedure eligibility assessment retains clinical examination and judgement time in this design.

assumptions: The task boundary is eligibility evaluation rather than booking, procedure execution or a separate note-writing task.
The clinical record system {OTHER} supplies existing history; the dermatologist verifies its relevance and obtains missing information within this full-time assessment.
No automated suitability rule, inferred contraindication flag or new diagnostic device is proposed.
Existing tools remain, with no new automation upkeep.
unknowns: Procedure mix and current assessment arrangements
research_questions: What information-assembly burden, if any, occurs outside the required individual assessment?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net 0. Examination, risk assessment and patient discussion remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Own specialist clinical judgement, trainee development and scientifically valid dermatology research.
reach: Help family medicine clinicians frame referral questions
role.ambitious_version: A dermatologist who protects time for patient assessment, colleague advice, trainee feedback and research judgement while identifying specific administrative work separately before automating it.
